pages.text: $(li)$(item)Transmitter Dish$()$(br)$(li)$(item)Receiver Dish$()$(br)$(li)$(item)Range Module I$()$(br)$(li)$(item)Range Module II$()$(br)$(li)$(item)Range Module III$()$(br)$(li)$(item)Infinity Range Module$()

Dishes send $(l)FE through the air$(), where a conduit can't go. There is no beam: you can tell a $(l)Transmitter Dish$() is working because it turns to a receiver and $(l)holds still$() while it sends, and a $(l)Receiver Dish$() is getting power because the rings of its dish $(l)light up$() from the rim to the centre.

$(li)It is a small multiblock: place it with $(l)three Cyber Frames$(), to its right, behind it and in the corner between, and the dish unfolds on its turret over a 2x2 base.$(br)$(li)Feed it FE with $(l:cables/energy_conduit)Energy Conduits$(/l) on the dish block.
pages.title: Transmitter Dish

pages.text: $(li)Each Transmitter Dish has $(l)one network$(). In its GUI you give it a $(l)name$() and a $(l)colour$(), which lights the indicator on both dishes.$(br)$(li)A new network is $(l)Private$(): only you and the players on your team can see it. Switch it to $(l)Public$() and anyone can link a receiver.

$(li)It serves up to $(l)4 receivers in turn$(): it turns to one, sends, then moves to the next. The signal passes through blocks, but the receiver's chunk must be loaded.$(br)$(li)A tenth of the FE is $(l)lost on the way$().

$(li)A small multiblock two blocks tall: put $(l)a Cyber Frame on top$() of it and its dish unfolds.$(br)$(li)Its GUI lists the networks it can reach, with their colour, distance (or dimension) and seats taken, for example "2/4". Click one to link; a full network is greyed out.
pages.title: Receiver Dish

pages.text: $(li)It gives the FE it receives to the blocks and conduits around it.

The Transmitter Dish has one module slot. The module sets how far it reaches and how much FE per tick it sends in all, shared among its receivers.$(br)$(li)$(l)None$(): 32 blocks, 2,000$(br)$(li)$(l)Range Module I$(): 128 blocks, 8,000$(br)$(li)$(l)Range Module II$(): 512 blocks, 32,000
pages.title: Range Modules

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Range Module III$(): 2,048 blocks, 128,000$(br)$(li)$(l)Infinity Range Module$(): Unlimited, into other dimensions, Unlimited$(br)With a receiver in another dimension, both dishes point $(l)straight up at the sky$().
